fields.label: giant dianoga feeler
fields.description: Thin, blind and slow, one of the giant dianoga's seven suckered tentacles, rising out of a still pool to search the shore after any loud noise. A dianoga hears everything. Harmless on its own; it is the one you see most, and the first sign that something enormous is paying attention. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: giant dianoga snare
fields.description: Thick, fast and gripping: a dianoga's tentacles are suckered, and this one shows why. It reaches for whatever wades too close and drags it toward the water. The killer of the six, and the reason nothing drinks at these pools unbothered. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: giant dianoga lash
fields.description: Long and barbed. The giant dianoga, many times the size of the trash squids of a city's sewers, carries barbed tentacles, and this limb is why that matters. It never grips; it strikes at maximum reach and withdraws, punishing anyone who lingers at the margin rather than crossing it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: giant dianoga porter
fields.description: More slender and delicate than its kin: a courier, not a hunter. Dianoga eat anything, fish and bones and refuse alike, and this tentacle rises just long enough to set down at the water's edge whatever the giant stripped from its last meal. Shoot it and the pool goes quiet on you forever; it never brings anything again. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: giant dianoga sentinel
fields.description: Motionless, raised just above the water. It does nothing; it listens. Dianoga have excellent hearing, and while this one is up the whole crown's chorus above falls silent to watch it. That silence is the loudest warning the Fever Wood has. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: giant dianoga eyestalk
fields.description: Vast. It does not reach; it opens. The giant dianoga's toothed maw gapes below, and above it the red eyestalk, as long as any of its tentacles, rises clear of the water. For one long moment the eye beneath the Fever Wood is exposed, and the eyestalk is the only place it can truly be hurt. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dianoga
fields.description: Dianoga originated on the planet Vodran and were large cephalopods capable of growing to great sizes. They had a single eyestalk protruding from their mollusk-like bodies, and seven suckered tentacles surrounding a fanged maw containing a sharp serrated probe. Normally these creatures were restricted to bodies of water, but this variety seems just as comfortable dragging itself around on land. RimMandrake: SW — Bestiary

fields.label: murrelith plumage
fields.description: Flat, translucent ribbon-plumes sheared from a murrelith's tail rather than plucked — they keep their colour and translucency long after the bird has grown a new set. Fetches a real price at market, which is exactly the problem: a colony living off the crown's silence is one bad trade away from a smaller warning. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: the Fever Wood
fields.description: The place where trees finally won. Great solid trunks, much more than one tile wide, have rooted the backswamp still and solid, tamed the flowing waters into shallow surface pools with deep, deep mud beneath. Their arches and branches have grown into byways well above the dark still pools -- roads made of living wood. In the crown: a whole arboreal world. Below: the black mirrors, unrippled. Nothing goes in the water here. Everything remembers why. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: captivity memory
fields.description: This animal was once held in a prison tank and broke free. Whatever the encounter is meant to cost it in the wild — its willingness to ever trust a hand again — is not yet tuned; the fact of it is remembered here. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: bound in kurreth paste
fields.description: Wrapped tight in a drying paste the kurreth spit, legs folded under. It is alive and unhurt, and cannot move until someone cuts it free. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: staked as lure
fields.description: Chained down at a lure stake, wounded and unable to break free. Whatever finds it first is not going to check whether it agreed to this. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: sap-sealed
fields.description: Bothered, this animal has flooded and set its own shell in hardened sap. It must be cracked open before anything more can be done to it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: swollen
fields.description: Bothered, this animal has inflated until it cannot be pulled from its perch. Bursting it now would yield a large one-time harvest — and end this animal as a renewable source for good. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: bough-soil
fields.description: A living bed of silt and scale-mat, thick along the boughways and heaped where the trunks crown out — the only ground in the Fever Wood's canopy where anything can put down roots. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: boughway
fields.description: A living lane grown across the crown — bark and root woven flat and firm well above the black pools below. Fast, safe, and never quite where the map says it was last season. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: black mirror pool
fields.description: Still, black water, deep and unrippled. Big animals wander in to drink and are sometimes simply gone. Nothing sane touches it, and nothing explains why. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: stilt platform
fields.description: A heavy timber platform raised on driven piles, built to carry real weight over ground the marsh itself refuses. Costlier than a plain bridge deck, and worth every log — this is the only way to build heavy structures at ground level in the Fever Wood. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: kurreth resin plug
fields.description: Chewed earth and hardened resin, packed into a tunnel by kurreth workers in moments. It will crumble on its own in a few hours; anything in a hurry has to break it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: lure stake
fields.description: A stout post driven into the ground, chain coiled at its base. Whatever gets tied here is meant to be found — by whatever is hunting nearby. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dianoga prison tank
fields.description: A sealed, waterlogged cell, not a pen. Whatever is inside it did not agree to be there and is strong enough that it never has to — the tank holds because it is built to, not because the occupant tolerates it. Fed, it will produce; neglected or breached, it will not stay. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: fever trunk core
fields.description: The living heart of a giant trunk — the one cell of it that never goes still, and never mines out. Everything the tree does starts here, at a pace this whole biome shares. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: fever trunk heartwood
fields.description: The outer mass of a giant trunk, grown dense and still over the still water below — packed tight enough to dig into like stone. Cut a chamber into it and it heals, slower than the Greentide's own boles ever did; this biome does everything slowly. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: craft radioactive suppressant charge
fields.description: Machine raw Uranium down into a sealed charge that goes unstable fast once exposed — dump one into a Fever Wood pool to drive whatever lives beneath it down for days. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: murrelith plumage
fields.description: Flat, translucent ribbon-plumes sheared from a murrelith's tail rather than plucked — they keep their colour and translucency long after the bird has grown a new set. Fetches a real price at market, which is exactly the problem: a colony living off the crown's silence is one bad trade away from a smaller warning. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: thavrik egg (unfert.)
fields.description: An unfertilized thavrik egg, taken from a guarded nest high in the crown. Edible raw, much better cooked. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: thavrik egg (fert.)
fields.description: A fertilized thavrik egg. Left undisturbed, it hatches into a chick — taken instead, it is one less reason for the adults to still be circling. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: radioactive suppressant charge
fields.description: A sealed charge of processed Uranium, machined to go unstable fast and diffuse into whatever it is dumped into. Foul a Fever Wood pool with one and whatever lives beneath it goes quiet for days — the free-tier answer to a threat the campaign world only ever meets with rarer, more dangerous salvage. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: thornbug nectar
fields.description: Sweet, thick nectar wept by a calm thornbug — the dairy the arboreal cantons run on. A frightened herd dries up for days; every raid on the guild costs nectar before it costs blood. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vaulm lacquer
fields.description: Amber-hard resin, cracked from a sealed vaulm's own shell. It sets glass-smooth and takes a fine finish — a real crafting material, and the reason anyone bothers a defended sap-sucker at all. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: drommath sap
fields.description: A thin trickle of sugar-sap, drawn off a swelling drommath without pushing it to burst. Renewable, for as long as the animal is left alone. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: burst drommath sap
fields.description: A gluttonous payout of sap, all at once, from a drommath burst rather than milked — this animal will never yield again. Worth far more than a season of the trickle it used to give. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dianoga spleen chemicals
fields.description: A vial of thick, faintly luminous fluid drained from a captive dianoga's spleen. Brewed, it makes dianogan tea: served hot, mildly narcotic, a delicacy to Muuns, and it stains the drinker's lips purple and teeth black. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dianoga cream
fields.description: A pale, rich secretion harvested from a fed captive dianoga: the filling of the dianoga cream-filled donut. It spoils quickly, same as any dairy off any animal. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: severed tentacle flesh
fields.description: A length of thick, rubbery, suckered flesh, still faintly warm, cut from a tentacle of the giant dianoga beneath the Fever Wood's pools. Dianoga regrow lost limbs, eventually, on the animal, not in the pack. Traders who know the biome pay well for it; it renders into a rich meat and a strange, purple-tinged tea. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: mirror list
fields.description: A traders' ledger of which black pools have moved lately — ripples, silences, the mirrors that lied about where they were. Reading it marks the agitated pools on your map for a while. The list is a snapshot; the water keeps its own schedule. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: thulvane
fields.description: A colossal fused column of a tree, its base so broad it reads as several trunks grown together, rising past sight so its crown is simply a permanent green ceiling. Bark in wet vertical plates, black in the grooves, permanently damp. The biome's structural unit — the ceiling, the interlock that keeps anything from falling, and the body colonists mine rooms into. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: skethral
fields.description: Shorter and wider than a thulvane, and visibly reaching: its heavy limbs grow horizontally toward its neighbours and fuse where they meet, so two skethrals read as one arch. Bark smooth and pale at the joins, scarred where limbs have knitted. This is the tree that grows the boughway roads — the in-fiction reason the crown is interlocked at all. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: varnoth
fields.description: Rooted in a mirror pool itself, on a tripod of prop-roots clear of the surface, its trunk leaning out over the water. Its lower bark is stained and polished to a wet black by the pool. Nothing grows beneath it. Its timber is the best in the biome — and it stands inside the reach, so reward and hazard are the same object. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: plennith
fields.description: A dense low mat of overlapping grey-green scales lying directly along bark and bough, thickening into a spongy bed that visibly holds silt and rot. Reads as a surface, never as a plant. This is what makes the bough-soil — the crown's fertility is biological, not geological, and where plennith has run, other things can grow. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ossagrel
fields.description: A thick segmented cane clamped along a bough, each joint swollen and split, weeping clear syrup that glazes and crusts below it. The whole plant looks over-full, and the bark under it is sugared and crawling. The host the crown's sap-suckers drink from, and the sugar line for stills and nectar-liquor. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ossagrel sap
fields.description: Sugar-thick syrup wept from ossagrel canes. Distills into a rough liquor or ferments into nectar; the crown's own sap-suckers drink it straight from the plant. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: cistrel
fields.description: A tight rosette of stiff waxy leaves forming a cup at chest height, holding clear standing water you can see into — the only water on this map that is not black. Outer leaves rust-red, inner pale. The only safe water in the Fever Wood, where people and tame animals drink. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: maulith
fields.description: A crossbeam of stiff branches carrying a dense curtain of flat ribbon-leaves that falls to the walkway below, so the plant is a room with walls. Leaves olive above, silver-backed and always moving slightly. The concealment plant of the crown, and the boughway's privacy screen. Ribbon-leaf is cordage. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: verrow
fields.description: Few fronds, held high and thin, with heavy dull-skinned gourds hanging well below them on long stalks — the fruit is the visual mass, not the leaves. The crown's staple food, reachable from a boughway without climbing. Free calories that draw the crown's grazers, and then the things that wait for grazers. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: nubrith
fields.description: A low leathery dome on a squat stalk, glowing a steady warm amber downward onto the deck. The only natural light in the crown — deliberately warm, sitting beside the Wildsteam's steam-lamp gold rather than fighting it. A leaf that glows, not a mushroom. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: halquin
fields.description: Two broad blade-leaves lying flat and opposite against the trunk like a pressed specimen, dark and leathery, with a swollen joint between them that beads resin. The medicine — the resin is the biome's herbal medicine line, gathered by scraping, a safe patient crown-side income. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ammeth
fields.description: One stiff flat fan of fused leaf held in a single plane from a short base, so it reads as a panel from one side and a line edge-on — the only plant here whose silhouette changes with facing. Waxy, rain-shedding, pale underneath. Roofing and decking; the cheapest building material in the biome, cut but never felled. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: claithe
fields.description: A flat rosette of blunt grey leaves over a broad pale root-plate that lifts clear of the mud, caked in grey clay it has bound out of the water. The potter's clay is harvested from its root-plate — a raw-terrain resource turned into a plant you can find, judge and farm at the water's edge. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: potter's clay
fields.description: Grey river clay, bound and lifted clear of the mud by a claithe's own root-plate. Workable straight from the plant. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: corvath
fields.description: A single thick dark-purple spike standing alone out of the mud, glossy and swollen, obviously better fed than anything around it. Always solitary — never more than a few at one pool. It grows only where the thing below has fed. A pool ringed with corvath is an occupied pool: the botanical tell that makes the pools readable. Worthless by design — its whole value is as information. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: sodderel
fields.description: A lopsided spar of a tree, half its limbs already dead and black with water, leaning permanently toward the pool. Living growth only on the high side. It looks like a wreck and is not one — this is the biome's ordinary construction wood, since the towers cannot be felled and varnoth is lethal to reach. It reads as naturally half-dead, not diseased. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: seepril
fields.description: A low dull barrel of a stem sitting in its own iridescent slick, the rainbow film spreading a cell or two around its base. Leafless above; just the barrel and the sheen. The seep-oils gather around it — perfume, lubricant, fuel. Its rainbow is the planet's honest register: just oil, just useful. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: seep oil
fields.description: Iridescent oil gathered from around a seepril's base. Perfume, lubricant or fuel, depending on who wants it. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: skimmel
fields.description: A continuous pale-green film lying perfectly flat over the mud, indistinguishable from firm ground until it is stepped on. Its only tell is that it is too even — no texture, no debris, and it never grows on ground that is actually solid. Disguises the sink-mud beneath it. ⚠️ Deliberately deceptive to the eye — do not "fix" this into looking safer or less like ground. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: wanlith
fields.description: Sparse colourless stalks a knee high, translucent and unbranched, standing in loose groups. Almost no biomass. Reads as absence — the visual proof that the floor is starved of light. The ground's baseline cover, deliberately worth almost nothing. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: tullick
fields.description: A tight low whorl of dull ribbed leaves with the ground visibly domed beneath it by the tuber below. The ground's one real reward — a bulk starch for the people working the causeway. Digging it churns the mud around it, an honest small cost. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: giant leaf
fields.description: An enormous, glossy leaf that grows low in the jungle understory, broad enough to shelter a grown man from the rain. Edible when young, and gathered as much for the shade as the food. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: giant leaf
fields.description: A giant and very impressive leaf. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: chellow
fields.description: Squat and round, with no feathers on its head at all — bare wrinkled skin and a translucent throat-fan it inflates to call, veined and lit faintly from behind. Easy to win over and easy to keep, a cultivated flock of chellow makes a private chorus outside the walls: as long as they are calling, the water below is quiet. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: murrelith
fields.description: Long-tailed, with flat translucent ribbons trailing where vaned quills should be — they hang and twist rather than spread. Those ribbons are worth real money, and that is exactly the temptation the crown sets against itself: sell the plumage and you have sold part of your own early warning. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: thavrik
fields.description: Heavy-bodied and short-winged, covered in coarse hair rather than feathers everywhere but the flight surfaces — a furred thing that flies. It nests high in the crown, eggs and nest material guarded by the adults: a reason to climb, if you can get past them. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: skellick
fields.description: Small and long-limbed, its plumes crumpled and unequal, sticking out at wrong angles as if damaged on purpose — the untidiest silhouette in the crown. It has learned to slip down and take small unattended things while nobody is looking, and it is very good at not being looked at. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: glomvar
fields.description: A pale, eyeless, many-legged thing the size of a calf, its soft back slick with a film that smells exactly like a kurreth hive. The ants walk past it, over it, feed their young beside it, and never notice that their numbers keep shrinking. It eats one a day. When the hive is busy fighting something else, it eats more. It has no interest in anything that is not a kurreth. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: kurreth
fields.description: A glossy red-black segmented ant the size of a large dog, oversized mandibles held forward as if perpetually mid-haul. Alone it is dangerous but not much of a threat; a whole hive of them is why nothing sensible digs where they have already dug. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: kurreth queen
fields.description: Vastly larger than any worker, sluggish outside her chamber, and never alone — a kurreth hive's queen is found only in its deepest room, worker escort pressed close around her. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: thornbug
fields.description: A great thorn-shaped insect clamped flush to the bark, secreting sweet, nourishing nectar in exchange for safety. The mechanic is the deal: it yields only while it feels safe, and a frightened herd dries up for days. Every raid on the crown costs nectar before it costs blood. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: vaulm
fields.description: A smooth swollen bead of amber on the bark, no limbs visible. Bothered, it floods its own shell and sets — armour, not flesh — and must be cracked open before anything more can be done to it. Killing and cracking it open yields a usable lacquer. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: ollareth
fields.description: Flat, wide, and ringed with open spiracles — bothered, it screams, and the whole crown answers. It yields nothing of its own; its value is that the biome fights for it, turning a theft raid into a fight the crown joins on your side. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: drommath
fields.description: A taut grey sac, visibly inflating. Handled, it swells rather than yield, until it cannot be pulled from its perch. Left calm, it can be milked for a small trickle of sap; burst instead, it pays out once, large — and never again. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: dianoga
fields.description: A young dianoga: a small, dark, seven-tentacled thing with a single eyestalk, kept in tanks because nothing else keeps it. It is not the giant beneath the Fever Wood's pools, not yet, but it is unmistakably kin to it, and everyone who has heard a dianoga hum up close swears they will never mistake the sound again. RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes

fields.label: captivity memory

designators.description:
Mark animals to be hunted by your hunters.

Only hunters with suitable ranged weapons will hunt.

designators.label: Slaughter
designators.description: Slaughter a tame animal.

designators.label: Tame
designators.description: Tame a wild animal.

designators.label: Haul things
designators.description: Mark rock chunks and other items to be hauled to dumping areas. Not needed for things like food or corpses, which are always haulable.

designators.label: Claim
designators.description: Claim neutral structures for the colony, including ancient ruins and abandoned siege bases. Claimed structures can be repaired and maintained by your colonists.

designators.label: Allow selection
designators.description:
Unforbid all items in the selected area.
Click and drag over an area to use.

designators.label: Forbid selection
designators.description:
Forbid all items in the selected area.
Click and drag over an area to use.

designators.label: Chop all wood
designators.description: Marks trees to be chopped down for wood regardless of growth level.

designators.label: Harvest all
designators.description: Marks harvestable plants to be harvested regardless of growth level.

designators.label: Chop grown wood
designators.description: Marks fully grown trees to be chopped down for wood.

designators.label: Harvest grown
designators.description: Marks fully grown plants to be harvested for their food or other products.

designators.label: Cut blighted
designators.description: Cut only blighted plants

designators.label: Cut grown
designators.description: Marks fully grown plants to be cut and destroyed. The plant will be completely removed, and any food or resource yield will be harvested.

designators.label: Strip Mine
designators.description: Mine a grid rather than everything

designators.label: Finish off
designators.description: Toggle finishing off

designators.label: Select similar
designators.description: Selects items similar to those already selected

designators.label: Haul urgently
designators.description: Mark rock chunks and other items to be hauled to dumping areas. Not needed for things like food or corpses, which are always haulable.

designators.label: Allow everything
designators.description: Unforbids all forbidden items on the map. Click to activate. Hold Ctrl/Option to include buildings. Hold Shift to include skeletons and non-fresh corpses.

designators.label: Select similar
designators.description: Selects only things similar to those already selected. Hold Shift to pick additional things. Hold Alt to ignore selection limits.

designators.label: Haul urgently
designators.description: Mark things to be hauled as soon as possible. Colonists will delay other work until hauling is complete. Configurable in the Work tab. Hold Shift to interrupt current colonist work.

designators.label: Finish off
designators.description: Quickly and painlessly kill downed creatures. Hold Shift to include colonists and allies. Requires a colonist with a melee skill of 6 or higher to use.

designators.label: Harvest fully grown
designators.description: Orders the harvesting or chopping crops and trees that are sufficiently grown to yield their maximum amount of resources when gathered. Hold Shift to include only plants. Hold Ctrl/Option to include only trees.

designators.label: Strip mine
designators.description: Lays out mine orders in a grid to maximize the chance to find hidden ores. Hold Shift to show settings window or designate using current settings.

designators.label: Smooth surface
designators.description: Designate rough stone terrain and walls to be smoothed.

designators.label: Paint building...
designators.description: Designate walls and buildings to be painted using dye from tinctoria plants, which you can grow. Only certain buildings can be painted.

designators.label: Paint floor...
designators.description: Designate floors to be painted using dye from tinctoria plants, which you can grow. Only certain floors can be painted.

designators.label: Remove paint
designators.description: Remove paint from walls, buildings, and floors.

designators.label: Plan
designators.description:
Place planning designations. These don't do anything except help you plan future expansions.

Right-click to hide or unhide all planning zones.

designators.label: Remove plans
designators.description: Remove planning designations.

designators.label: Export
designators.description: Export a building to xml

designators.label: Export from area
designators.description: Export a building to xml from area

designators.label: Destroy item
designators.description: Burns chosen item at closest campfire, destroying it completely. Requires campfire or smelter to work.

designators.label: Designator route
designators.description: Designator route desc

designators.label: constructed roof
designators.description: Set a roof or terrain within the specified range.

designators.label: bridge
designators.description: Set a roof or terrain within the specified range.

designators.label: Spawn: Wood
designators.description:
Wood from trees or other fibrous plants. Useful for building structures and weapons. It is a good fuel for campfires and generators, and can be refined into chemfuel. In a pinch, a piece of wood can be used as a weapon or a leg.
Tip: Right click to open the menu and select the thing to generate.

designators.label: move out
designators.description: Mark items that need to be moved out from the sub map, pay attention! Only when the target map is a sub map of a certain map can it be used.

designators.label: Move in submap（No Submap）
designators.description: Mark items that need to be moved into the sub map, pay attention! It can only be used when there is a target sub map.

designators.label: <color=#75BBFDFF>Pawn spawner</color>
designators.description:
Used to generate pawns.
Tip: Right click to select a custom thing.

designators.label: <color=#75BBFDFF>Trap editor</color>
designators.description: <color=#75BBFDFF>Used to edit traps.</color>

designators.label: Set faction: Null
designators.description: Set the faction for selected things.

designators.label: Set style:Null
designators.description: Set the style for selected things.

designators.label: Set hit points: 100%
designators.description: Set the hit points of selected things. Right click to switch modes.

designators.label: Set quality: Normal
designators.description: Set the quality of selected things. Right click to switch between fixed, upgrade, and downgrade modes.

designators.label: Set plant maturity: 100%
designators.description: Set the maturity of selected plants. Right click to adjust maturity.

designators.label: Set item count: 1
designators.description: Set the stack count of selected items. Right click to switch between custom and adjustment modes.

designators.label: Blueprint
designators.description: Place custom map blueprints. Right click to open the floating blueprint palette.

designators.label: Batch pasting(Loot box)
designators.description: Paste the copied data into a selected thing.

designators.label: Save Zone: Circular
designators.description: Select a circular zone to save as a custom map def.(Only applicable to saving map part. If saving a whole map, please use Save Whole Map)

designators.label: Disgenerate
designators.description: Mark the area, and the zone core will not generate the "map part" in the disgenerate area.

designators.label: Disdestroy
designators.description: Mark the area, and when generating custom map data, the thing within the area will not be destroyed.

designators.label: Custom lord
designators.description: Customize lord within the map, lord data will be saved in the custom map def

designators.label: Destroy Item
designators.description: Order a pawn to destroy this item

designators.label: Paint graffiti here
designators.description: Mark a wall cell for a colonist to paint graffiti on, next time one is free.

designators.label: Destroy item
designators.description: Burns chosen item at closest campfire, destroying it completely. Requires campfire or smelter to work.

designators.label: Recycle item
designators.description: Recycle chosen item to get valuables resources out of it. If item can be smelted it will require smelter to get recycled, otherwise it will be scrapped on it's location.

designators.label: Destroy item
designators.description: Burns chosen item at closest campfire, destroying it completely. Requires campfire or smelter to work.

designators.label: Recycle item
designators.description: Recycle chosen item to get valuables resources out of it. If item can be smelted it will require smelter to get recycled, otherwise it will be scrapped on it's location.

designators.label: Rearm Traps
designators.description: Designate traps to be rearmed by colonists.

designators.label: Open
designators.description: Open containers.

designators.label: Apply deepfire
designators.description: Mark a wall, floor furniture, art piece, apparel or weapon for a colonist to coat in deepfire. Colour comes from however it is currently painted; deepfire adds the glow. Up to three coats, each brightening the light.

designators.label: Remove deepfire
designators.description: Strip all deepfire coats from a wall, floor furniture, art piece, apparel or weapon at once. No refund.

designators.label: Dig canal
designators.description: Carve a channel one level deeper. Designating a channel that is already dug deepens it again — shallow, mid, deep, then SUPERDEEP. Liquid fills the deepest cells first and overflows into shallower ones. A channel dug into the strip along the map edge is a SINK: liquid reaching it leaves the map, which is how you empty a canal on purpose.

designators.label: Fill in canal
designators.description: Fill an excavated cell back in by one level. Liquid that no longer fits is pushed into the rest of the channel and back into the body it came from; only what finds no room anywhere is lost. Filling a cell all the way back to the surface restores the terrain that was there before it was dug.

designators.label: Stake as lure
designators.description: Flag a tamed animal or prisoner to be staked as living bait for the Fever Wood's raiders. It will be wounded down and chained in the open — there is no bloodless version of this.

designators.label: Foul pool with suppressant
designators.description: Mark a Fever Wood pool cell to be fouled with a radioactive suppressant charge (crafted from Uranium). A colonist will carry a charge there and dump it, driving whatever lives beneath the pool down for several days — no hostile encounters and no treasure trickle from that pool while it lasts.

designators.label: Paint Tool
designators.description: Paint buildings, apparel and terrain
